explanation: Generators must maintain a dynamic reactive power capability between 0.95 leading and 0.95 lagging at the high-side of the substation to ensure grid stability.

source: NOPR Proposal, Section C. Real Power Output Level 1
explanation: Non-synchronous generators must maintain required power factor range only when real power output exceeds 10% of their nameplate capacity.

Inverters used by non-synchronous generators cannot produce reactive power when operating below 10% of nameplate capacity.

source: SGIA, Order No. 661, FERC Stats. & Regs. ¶ 31,186 at P 46
explanation: Non-synchronous generators must maintain power factor when output exceeds 10% of nameplate capacity to ensure grid stability.
